text:
leo.sales: Maria from GroveBank wants clarity on BYO-HSM options for their POC. Key asks: split custody for root CMK, automated rewraps every 30m, and whether rewraps will bump request/throughput charges. Need short answer + a SOW bullet for presales.

maria.cto: Correct. We need two-person custody for CMK import (our vault + Redwood operator), automated rewrap to fresh DEKs every 30 minutes, and clear billing expectations. Also need to know if we can throttle rewraps during peak.

sam.crypto: We support split custody import flows. Our import uses an envelope-wrapping process: customer provides a wrapped CMK, we unwrap in the HSM under dual-operator approval, then store a key handle in the customer partition. Rewraps are derived DEKs (data encryption keys) generated server-side and wrapped by the CMK.

sam.crypto: Rewrap cadence: 30m TTL is OK but note operational cost: each rewrap is a crypto operation inside the HSM (HKDF + wrap). That incurs CloudHSM RPCs or on-prem HSM ops. No need to re-import CMK.

sam.crypto: Pseudo-config: 
```
key_policy:
  custody: split
  import_mode: dual-approval
  rewrap:
    mode: automated-derived
    interval_minutes: 30
    retain_count: 48
```

vijay.eng: Infra note: rewraps generate key-management API calls and metric events. For 2000 QPS we should expect roughly 2000 wrap calls/sec (one per encryption) plus rewrap throughput spikes at the 30m boundary if many tenants align. We recommend jittering rewrap schedules per-tenant to avoid pileups.

vijay.eng: If you prefer hard windows, we can provide a rolling rewrap (staggered by tenant ID hash) — no infra change needed, just config.

naya.sec: Security/CSP note: audit trail will log every wrap/unwrap and rewrap. For split custody we produce an import manifest signed by both operators. We can produce an attestation PDF for the SOW showing the custody flow and HSM serials.

legal-bot: Standard POC addendum template updated with BYO split-custody language: https://legal.example.com/templates/byo-split-custody-poc-v2.pdf

leo.sales: Maria, billing implications: rewraps themselves are not charged per-token, but they increase HSM operations and API call counts which factor into the POC cost. Two pricing flows: CloudHSM path (pay cloud HSM hourly + ops) vs On-prem HSM proxy (one-time eng integration + runbook fee). Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) recommended if you expect peak load > 1k QPS during the POC.

maria.cto: Can you give a ballpark for HSM ops at 2000 QPS with 30m rewrap and 48 retained DEKs? Also tell us how rewrap jittering reduces peaks.

sam.crypto: Ballpark: 2000 QPS => ~2000 wrap ops/sec. If DEKs are derived per-request at that rate, expect ~173M wrap ops/day. Cloud HSM will charge per-hour and has API quotas; estimate depends on vendor. Rewraps: 2000 tenants aligned at 30m boundary => 2000 extra wrap ops at that minute (negligible vs sustained QPS). Jittering distributes that 2000 across 1800 seconds (30m), adding ~1 extra op/sec on average per-tenant group. So pileup risk is low if we apply tenant jitter.

vijay.eng: Implementation option to reduce HSM ops: enable local key cache for DEKs with TTL slightly under rewrap interval and perform wrap/unwrap in batches. This trades memory for fewer HSM calls. We'll propose a cache config in the POC sketch.

leo.sales: Action items: 1) Sam to add split-custody import flow diagram + attestation language; 2) Vijay to add jittering and cache-suggestion notes + rough cost model; 3) Legal to review addendum link and return a redline.

deploy-bot: POC env rwd-poc-grove-01 created. Invite sent to maria.cto, leo.sales.

legal-bot: ETA for redline 48 hours; will include SOW clause for key escrow refusal and operator access controls.

maria.cto: Thanks team. If you can include an explicit example cost-row for CloudHSM hourly + Redwood integration fee that would help our procurement.

leo.sales: Will include a simple three-line cost table in the POC quote (CloudHSM hourly, Redwood integration/runbook, Dedicated pool trial if requested). Expect draft in 36h. :white_check_mark:
